greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ λιμὸς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς χωρὶς τοῦ λιμοῦ τοῦ πρότερον, ὃς ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τῷ Αβρααμ· ἐπορεύθη δὲ Ισαακ πρὸς Αβιμελεχ βασιλέα Φυλιστιιμ εἰς Γεραρα.
hint: A famine comes on the land, besides the earlier famine in Abraham's time; Isaac goes to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

notes.text: χωρίς is first *separately, asunder, apart*; πρότερος, the positive Middle Liddell heads, with the repeated article.
The article repeated before the name, which is genitive: `the`, as at 24:52.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐγενήθη for the second ἐγένετο, and τοῦ for the second τῷ, where the Berlin papyrus, 911, has τῷ.

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")
(Ισαακ, from Hebrew Yiṣḥāq, "he laughs")
(Αβιμελεχ, from Hebrew ʾĂbîmelek, "my father is king")
(Φυλιστιιμ, from Hebrew Pĕlištîm, a people of the Hebrew plural in -îm)
(Γεραρα, from Hebrew Gĕrār, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν Μὴ καταβῇς εἰς Αἴγυπτον· κατοίκησον δὲ ἐν τῇ γῇ, ᾗ ἄν σοι εἴπω.
hint: The Lord appears to him and says: Do not go down to Egypt; settle in the land I tell you of.

notes.text: ὁράω in the passive, the chain of GEN 12:7.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: καὶ παροίκει ἐν τῇ γῇ ταύτῃ, καὶ ἔσομαι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ εὐλογήσω σε· σοὶ γὰρ καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου δώσω πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ταύτην καὶ στήσω τὸν ὅρκον μου, ὃν ὤμοσα Αβρααμ τῷ πατρί σου.
hint: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; to you and to your offspring I will give all this land, and I will keep the oath I swore to Abraham your father.

notes.text: ἵστημι, the chain of GEN 6:18; ὅρκος, the chain of 21:14, in the accusative.
παροικέω, the chain of GEN 21:23, in the imperative.

hint: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven, and give your offspring all this land, and in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed,

notes.text: The verse repeats 22:17–18 word for word; the chains are those verses'.

greek: ἀνθʼ ὧν ὑπήκουσεν Αβρααμ ὁ πατήρ σου τῆς ἐμῆς φωνῆς καὶ ἐφύλαξεν τὰ προστάγματά μου καὶ τὰς ἐντολάς μου καὶ τὰ δικαιώματά μου καὶ τὰ νόμιμά μου.
hint: because Abraham your father listened to my voice and kept my charges, my commandments, my statutes and my customs.

greek: καὶ κατῴκησεν Ισαακ ἐν Γεραροις.
hint: So Isaac settles in Gerar.

notes.text: Γεραρα declines as a neuter plural, as at 20:1.

reading: and [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate|κατοικέω]] [[name:Ισαακ]] in [[name:Γεραροις]].

greek: Ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου περὶ Ρεβεκκας τῆς γυναικὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν Ἀδελφή μού ἐστιν· ἐφοβήθη γὰρ εἰπεῖν ὅτι Γυνή μού ἐστιν, μήποτε ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου περὶ Ρεβεκκας, ὅτι ὡραία τῇ ὄψει ἦν.
hint: The men of the place ask about Rebekah his wife, and he says, She is my sister; he was afraid to say, She is my wife, in case the men of the place should kill him over Rebekah, because she was fair to look on.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ πολυχρόνιος ἐκεῖ· παρακύψας δὲ Αβιμελεχ ὁ βασιλεὺς Γεραρων διὰ τῆς θυρίδος εἶδεν τὸν Ισαακ παίζοντα μετὰ Ρεβεκκας τῆς γυναικὸς αὐτοῦ.
hint: He is there a long time; and Abimelech king of Gerar looks out through the window and sees Isaac playing with Rebekah his wife.

notes.text: πολυχρόνιος, *long-existing, of olden time, ancient*, of the time he spent there.
παρακύπτω is first *to stoop sideways*.

hint: Abimelech calls Isaac and says: So she is your wife; why did you say, She is my sister? Isaac says: I said it in case I should die because of her.

greek: καὶ ἐποίησεν αὐτοῖς δοχήν, καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἔπιον·
hint: He makes them a feast, and they eat and drink;

notes.text: δοχή, *a receiving, reception*, of a banquet.

reading: and [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced, performed, did|ποιέω]] to them [[a receiving|a receiving, a reception, an entertainment, a feast|δοχή]], and [[they ate|they ate, they ate of|ἐσθίω]] and [[they drank|they drank, they drank of, they drank up|πίνω]];

greek: καὶ ἀναστάντες τὸ πρωὶ ὤμοσαν ἄνθρωπος τῷ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς Ισαακ, καὶ ἀπῴχοντο ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ μετὰ σωτηρίας.
hint: and rising early they swear to one another; Isaac sends them off, and they go from him in safety.

notes.text: *A man to his neighbour*, the Hebrew idiom *ʾîš lĕrēʿēhû*; πλησίον after the article, as at 11:3.
ἀποίχομαι, *to be gone away, be absent*.

reading: and [[having stood up|having stood up, having risen, having risen to fight against, having risen to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] the [[early in the day|early in the day, early, at morn, betimes, in good time, too soon and too early|πρωΐ]] [[swore|swore, swore to and affirmed and confirmed by oath, swore that one would, swore by|ὄμνυμι]] [[man|a man, a human being, mankind|ἄνθρωπος]] [[to the neighbour|to the neighbour, to the one near and close to and neighbouring, to the one nigh and hard by, to one's neighbour|πλησίον]] of him, and [[sent quite away|sent quite away, dispatched|ἐξαποστέλλω]] them [[name:Ισαακ]], and [[were gone away|were gone away, were absent and away, had departed|ἀποίχομαι]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] him [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of a saving|of a saving, of deliverance, of preservation, of safety, of a safe return, of a keeping safe, of security and a guarantee for safety|σωτηρία]].

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ παραγενόμενοι οἱ παῖδες Ισαακ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ περὶ τοῦ φρέατος, οὗ ὤρυξαν, καὶ εἶπαν Οὐχ εὕρομεν ὕδωρ.
hint: That same day Isaac's servants come and tell him about the well they had dug, and say: We have not found water.

notes.text: παραγίνομαι, *to come to be beside, come up, arrive*.
The relative drawn into the genitive after φρέατος.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[in the day|within, inside of, and by means of the day, the day-break, the time|ἡμέρα]] [[that|that, the one there, the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]] and [[having come to be beside|having come to be beside, having come up and arrived, having come to help, having been present, having stood by|παραγίνομαι]] [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids|παῖς]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[brought tidings|brought tidings, reported, announced, carried a report, related and narrated|ἀπαγγέλλω]] to him [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very|περί + genitive]] [[of the well|of the well, of the tank and cistern and reservoir, of the oil jar|φρέαρ]], of which [[dug|dug, dug through, dug up|ὀρύσσω]], and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] not [[we found|we found, we found out, we discovered|εὑρίσκω]] water.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸ Ὅρκος· διὰ τοῦτο ὄνομα τῇ πόλει Φρέαρ ὅρκου ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
hint: He calls it Oath; and so the city's name is Well of the Oath to this day.

notes.text: The Greek words printed as names: the Hebrew is Šibʿâ and Bĕʾēr Šebaʿ, Beersheba, as at 21:31.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ for αὐτό, and puts ἐκάλεσεν τό before ὄνομα; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has neither.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] it [[name:Ὅρκος]]; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[to the city|to the city, to the citadel, to the country, to the body of citizens, to the state|πόλις]] [[name:Φρέαρ]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath|ὅρκος]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as|ἕως]] the to-day [[of day|of day, of day-break, of time|ἡμέρα]].

names.gloss: (Ὅρκος, the Greek word ὅρκος, "the object by which one swears, oath", printed as the well's name; the Hebrew is Šibʿâ, "seven" or "oath")
(Φρέαρ ὅρκου, "well of the oath", the Greek of Hebrew Bĕʾēr Šebaʿ, Beersheba)

greek: Ἦν δὲ Ησαυ ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα καὶ ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα Ιουδιν τὴν θυγατέρα Βεηρ τοῦ Χετταίου καὶ τὴν Βασεμμαθ θυγατέρα Αιλων τοῦ Ευαίου.
hint: Esau was forty years old when he took as wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hivite.

notes.text: ἦν of age, the formula of GEN 1:2 in full, as at 25:20.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the first τήν and reads μασεμμαθ and αιλωμ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has ευλων for Αιλων.

reading: was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] of years forty and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] woman [[name:Ιουδιν]] the daughter [[name:Βεηρ]] [[name:Χετταίου]] and [[name:Βασεμμαθ]] daughter [[name:Αιλων]] [[name:Ευαίου]].

names.gloss: (Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair")
(Ιουδιν, for Hebrew Yĕhûdît, "Jewess" or "woman of Judah")
(Βεηρ, for Hebrew Bĕʾērî, usually connected with bĕʾēr, "well")
(Χετταῖος, the man of Χετ, Heth; Hebrew Ḥittî)
(Βασεμμαθ, from Hebrew Bāśĕmat, usually connected with bōśem, "balsam, spice")
(Αιλων, from Hebrew ʾÊlōn, usually connected with ʾēlôn, "oak, terebinth")
(Ευαῖος, the man of the people the Hebrew calls Ḥiwwî, the Hivite)

greek: καὶ ἦσαν ἐρίζουσαι τῷ Ισαακ καὶ τῇ Ρεβεκκα.
hint: And they were a strife to Isaac and to Rebekah.

notes.text: ἦν with the participle, the formula in its shorter form; ἐρίζω is first *to strive, wrangle, quarrel*.

reading: and were, and kept on being, [[striving|striving, wrangling, quarrelling, rivalling and vying with and being a match for, contending with, engaging in a contest and keeping the contest up|ἐρίζω]] to [[name:Ισαακ]] and to [[name:Ρεβεκκα]].
